lastText: File ClosedThe Fortress Meets the BombMajor DefeatWehrmacht High Command, 1939–1945End of hostilities: AUTUMN 1945 (PROJECTED) · filed late, out of sequenceImmediate AftermathThis was the war that never went east: the deepest projection this campaign contains, since no German planning document ever seriously mapped it: the regime's entire ideology pointed at the decision you cancelled. What followed was a siege, not a campaign. The army history destroyed in Russia ██████ intact and unused; the Soviet Union grew stronger every uncontested quarter; and the Anglo-American war arrived anyway, by air and by blockade, against industry it could reach and imports it █████ throttle. The retaliation campaign repeated the historical Reich's worst air-war trade, buying headlines with the fighters the defense needed but the strategic ████████ never changed, because it could not: the fortress had no way to reach the powers besieging it. The Suez axis delivered the most complete regional victory in this campaign, and demonstrated its own ceiling, since no Mediterranean conquest touched the Atlantic or the arithmetic behind it. The fortified truce held the eastern question at gunpoint: deterrence as permanent ███████████, the border war that never quite came defining a Europe armed to its median line.
